([[Canberra]], Australia) | college = [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] (2019–2022) | draftyear = 2022 | career_start = 2018 | career_end = | years1 = 2018–2019 | team1 = [[BA Centre of Excellence]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years3 = 2023–2025 | team3 = [[Illawarra Hawks]] | years4 = 2024 | team4 = [[Osaka Evessa]] | years5 = 2025–present | team5 = [[Nagasaki Velca]] | highlights = * [[List of NBL champions|NBL champion]] ([[2024–25 NBL season|2025]]) * First-team All-[[Atlantic 10]] (2022) * Atlantic 10 All-Rookie Team (2020) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|KOR}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Asia Under-16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2015 FIBA Asia Under-16 Championship|2015 Indonesia]]|[[South Korea men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Lee Hyun-jung''' (born October 23, 2000) is a South Korean professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson Wildcats]] of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] (A-10). He helped the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) win the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] in 2025. ==Early life and career== Lee attended Samil Commercial School in [[Suwon]], where he played basketball under the coaching of his father.{{cite web |title=Could Lee Hyunjung be the next Yuta Watanabe? Steph Curry's college coach thinks so |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/could-lee-hyunjung-be-the-next-yuta-watanabe-steph-currys-college-coach-thinks-so |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=December 21, 2020 |date=July 14, 2020}} In middle school, Lee was only {{convert|170|cm|ftin|sp=us}} and played as a [[Guard (basketball)|guard]], as he practiced dribbling and mid-range shooting. By the end of his middle school years, Lee grew to over {{convert|190|cm|ftin|sp=us}}. He played as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] during defense and a guard during the offense.{{Cite web |last=Yoo |first=Jee-ho |date=May 8, 2019 |title=S. Korean basketball prospect to join Davidson in NCAA |url=https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20190508000700315 |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=en}} He modeled his game after [[Klay Thompson]].{{cite web |last=Gershon |first=Josh |title=Hyunjung Lee: 2019 South Korean SF planning two official visits |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Hyunjung-Lee-recruiting-Davidson-Washington-State-131263135/ |website=[[247Sports]] |access-date=December 22, 2020 |date=April 16, 2019}} In 2018, Lee enrolled at the NBA Global Academy in [[Canberra]], Australia.{{cite web |last=Scott |first=David |title=From South Korea to Australia to Davidson: Hyunjung Lee's journey never lost sight of home |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article240362751.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=December 21, 2020 |date=February 17, 2020}} While at the academy, he played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL) in 2018 and then the [[NBL1]] in [[2019 NBL1 season|2019]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Hyunjung-Lee/376913|title=Hyunjung Lee|work=usbasket.com|access-date=June 27, 2023|url-access=subscription}} In conjunction with the NBA Global Academy and the Centre of Excellence, he attended [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra Secondary College]],{{cite web|url=https://davidsonwildcats.com/sports/basketball/roster/lee-hyunjung/8134|title=Hyunjung Lee|work=davidsonwildcats.com|access-date=June 27, 2023}} where he learned to speak [[English language|English]]. Lee committed to playing college basketball for [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] over an offer from [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]]. He drew the attention of head coach [[Bob McKillop]] and his staff at a [[Basketball Without Borders]] event. He would become the fourth player and the second men's player from South Korea to play [[NCAA Division I]] basketball.{{cite web |last=Yonhap |date=May 8, 2019 |title=Lee will be Korea's 4th NCAA Division I baller |url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/2019/05/08/Baseball/Lee-will-be-Koreas-4th-NCAA-Division-I-baller/3062789.html |access-date=December 21, 2020 |website=[[Korea JoongAng Daily]] |language=en}} ==College career== As a freshman with the [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson Wildcats]] in 2019–20, Lee appeared in 28 games off the bench and finished seventh among A-10 first-year players in scoring, averaging 8.4 points per game. On February 7, 2020, he scored a season-high 20 points in a 73–62 loss to [[2019–20 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]].{{cite web |date=February 7, 2020 |title=Rams Ride Wildcat Miscues to Win |url=https://davidsonwildcats.com/news/2020/2/7/mens-basketball-at-vcu.aspx |access-date=December 22, 2020 |website=Davidson College Athletics}} He was subsequently named to the Atlantic 10 All-Rookie Team.{{cite web |last=Scott |first=David |date=March 10, 2020 |title=Davidson's Kellan Grady, Jon Axel Gudmundsson make all-Atlantic 10 teams |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article241052126.html |access-date=December 22, 2020 |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230630115225/https://amp.charlotteobserver.com/article241052126.html |archive-date=June 30, 2023}} As a sophomore in 2020–21, Lee started all 22 games and finished second on the team in scoring and assists. He became the first-ever Wildcat to conclude the season shooting at least 50 percent overall, 40 percent from three-point range and 90 percent from the free throw line. He twice scored a season-high 23 points. He averaged 13.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game. As a junior in 2021–22, Lee played in 34 games and made 33 starts, averaging 15.8 points, 6.0 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. On December 1, 2021, he recorded a career-high 32 points and 14 rebounds against [[2021–22 Charlotte 49ers men's basketball team|Charlotte]].{{Cite web |title=Lee scores 32 to lift Davidson over Charlotte 75-58 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401370998 |access-date=June 30, 2023 |date=December 1, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web |title=Hyunjung Lee Game Log 2021-22 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/4592308/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2022 |access-date=June 30, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} He was subsequently named first-team All-Atlantic 10.{{Cite web |title=Brajkovic Named Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, McKillop, Osunniyi Earn Top Honors |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2022/3/8/mens-basketball-brajkovic-named-atlantic-10-player-of-the-year-mckillop-osunniyi-earn-top-honors.aspx |access-date=June 30, 2023 |date=March 8, 2022 |website=atlantic10.com}} On April 26, 2022, Lee declared for the [[2022 NBA draft|NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Yonhap |date=April 27, 2022 |title=S. Korean player Lee Hyun-jung declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220427000595 |access-date=January 3, 2023 |website=[[The Korea Herald]] |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2023)=== After suffering a foot injury,{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2022 |title=NBA draft hopeful Lee Hyun-jung likely out for months with foot injury |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/sports/2023/01/600_331573.html |access-date=January 3, 2023 |website=[[Korea Times]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Hyunjung Lee: On mend from foot injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hyunjung-lee-on-mend-from-foot-injury/ |access-date=January 3, 2023 |website=[[CBS Sports]] }} Lee went undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Yoo |first=Jee-ho |date=June 24, 2022 |title=S. Korean player Lee Hyun-jung goes undrafted in NBA |url=https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20220624005200315 |access-date=January 3, 2023 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=en}} On February 20, 2023, Lee was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|access-date=February 20, 2023}} In 12 games to complete the [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–23 season]], he averaged 5.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Hyunjung-Lee/Summary/108027|title=Hyunjung Lee|work=realgm.com|access-date=June 27, 2023}} Lee played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Hawks Welcome Korean Sharpshooter Hyunjung Lee|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/hawks-welcome-korean-sharpshooter-hyunjung-lee|work=Hawks.com.au|date=July 11, 2023|access-date=July 11, 2023}} ===Illawarra Hawks and Osaka Evessa (2023–2025)=== On July 11, 2023, Lee signed a three-year deal with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). On January 20, 2024, he scored a career-high 24 points on 5-of-8 three-point shooting in a 96–89 loss to the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/sixers-climb-off-bottom-hand-hawks-third-straight-loss|title=Sixers climb off bottom, hand Hawks third straight loss|work=NBL.com.au|date=January 20, 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240120131040/https://nbl.com.au/news/sixers-climb-off-bottom-hand-hawks-third-straight-loss|archive-date=January 20, 2024}} On March 19, 2024, Lee signed with the [[Osaka Evessa]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web |title=イ ヒョンジュン選手 契約基本合意(新規) |url=https://www.evessa.com/news/240319_01/ |website=大阪エヴェッサ |access-date=27 September 2024 |date=19 March 2024}} His contract expired on May 31, 2024.{{cite web |title=イ ヒョンジュン選手 契約満了 |url=https://www.evessa.com/news/240604_03/ |website=大阪エヴェッサ |access-date=27 September 2024 |date=5 June 2024}} Lee returned to the Illawarra Hawks for the [[2024–25 NBL season]] and helped the team win the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]].{{cite news |title="Lee for Three!": Hyunjung Lee Departs Hawks for Japan Opportunity |url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/lee-for-three-hyunjung-lee-departs-hawks-for-japan-opportunity |access-date=31 July 2025 |work=Illawarra Hawks {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=31 July 2025}} He parted ways with the Hawks in July 2025, after his contract was bought out by a Japanese club. In 69 games for the Hawks, he averaged 7.6 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.1 assists, connecting on 38% of his three-point attempts. ===Nagasaki Velca (2025–present)=== On July 30, 2025, Lee signed with the [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite news |title=イ ヒョンジュン 選手契約基本合意(新規)のお知らせ |url=https://www.velca.jp/news/detail/id=47702 |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=velca.jp |date=30 July 2025 |language=ja}} He helped the Velca win the championship and was named Championship MVP. For the [[2026 NBA Summer League]], Lee played for the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite news |title=최소 연봉 20억원. B. 리그 매력제안, 이현중은 NBA 도전을 선택했다. 샌안토니오 스퍼스 서머리그 입성 |url=https://www.chosun.com/english/sports-en/2026/06/04/BMD34PII6ZBLHHJOABENGYML4E/|date=2026-06-04|access-date=2026-07-16|website=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]| last=Ryu |first=Dong-hyuk |url-status=live |language=ko|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716083544/https://www.chosun.com/sports/basketball/2026/06/04/GIZDINLFGZQWCZJQMU4DCOJSMI/|archive-date=2026-07-16}} ==National team career== Lee played for [[South Korea men's national under-17 basketball team|South Korea's junior national team]] at the [[2015 FIBA Asia Under-16 Championship]]. He averaged 14 points and 5.7 rebounds per game, leading his team to its first gold medal at the tournament.{{cite web |date=November 7, 2015 |title=Korea power their way past Chinese Taipei for maiden FIBA Asia U16 title |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/asia/u16/2015/news/korea-power-their-way-past-chinese-taipei-for-maiden-fiba-asia-u16-title |access-date=December 22, 2020 |publisher=[[FIBA]]}}{{cite web |title=Hyunjung Lee (KOR)'s profile - FIBA Asia U16 Championship for Men 2015 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/asia/u16/2015/player/Hyunjung-Lee |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=December 22, 2020}} Lee represented South Korea at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] and [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Asian Championship]]. He averaged 26 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 6 assists per game at the 2018 tournament.{{cite web |title=Hyunjung Lee stats |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/asia/u18/2018/player/Hyunjung-Lee |website=FIBA |access-date=March 23, 2022}} He played for the senior team at the [[2020 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments]] and during the [[2022 FIBA Asia Cup qualification|2022 FIBA Asia Cup qualifiers]].{{cite web |date=May 11, 2021 |title=Davidson's Hyunjung Lee Selected to Senior National Team |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2021/5/11/mens-basketball-davidsons-hyunjung-lee-selected-to-senior-national-team.aspx |access-date=January 11, 2022 |website=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]}} ==Personal life== Lee's mother, [[Sung Jung-a]], won a silver medal while representing South Korea in basketball at the [[1984 Summer Olympics]]. His father, Lee Yoon-hwan, played semi-professionally before becoming a high school athletic director and coach. His older sister, Lee Ri-na, played for the South Korean under-16 national team.{{cite web |date=May 8, 2019 |title=S. Korean basketball prospect to join Davidson in NCAA. He has a girlfriend Rebecca Yeh. |url=https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20190508000700315 |access-date=December 21, 2020 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]]}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
